title: Rapid Handoff + Observability Checklist — Aug 02 2027
content:
TL;DR: Quiet day overall. Two small P2s (inference cache thrash & a degraded autoscaler sync) were handled with temporary mitigations; both require follow-up runbook edits. No customer-facing outages. Handing off to Liam for midnight -> 08:00 PST. Key things for next shift: watch prefix-cache saturation, autoscaler controller leader flapping, and one pending PR for a backoff change (infra PR #739).

Summary (high-level):
- Date: 2027-08-02 (Shift: 16:00–00:00 PST)
- Primary oncall: Maya Chen (me)
- Secondary: Priya Kapoor (available via phone)
- Coverage owner for night: Liam O'Neill (taking over at 00:00)
- Total alerts routed to oncall: 18 (8 informational, 9 SLO noise, 1 action-required)

Incident 1 — P2: inference-prefix-cache thrash (15:22–15:48)
- Symptoms: elevated tail latency on hosted API routes /v1/generate and increased token compute per request. Grafana: token/s per instance spike and KV cache evictions metric jumped from ~3% to 62%.
- First alert: 15:20 — alert name `svc-inference.cache-eviction-rate:high`
- Mitigation sequence performed:
  1) 15:22 — scaled up prefix-cache instances in region eu-west-1 (temp pool +3, cmd: kubectl scale deploy/prefix-cache -n inference --replicas=7) to absorb thrash.
  2) 15:30 — throttled aggressive client that was emitting long prompt sequences (identified via token-cost-tagging in logs). Contacted solutions-eng for owner mapping (Slack convo: #eng-solutions, thread ID Tsx9Z3).
  3) 15:36 — applied temporary prefix-cache TTL increase to reduce churn (feature flag: cache.prefix.ttl=600s).
- Root cause hypothesis: a new client-side SDK version (opt-in beta) introduced bursty prefix generation in a small set of customers; combined with cache TTL set to 60s caused eviction storms.
- Impact: P2; no SLO breach yet but risk of repeated spikes.
- Followups / Actions:
  * PR (infra) to add a higher TTL default for heavy-prefix routes: owner Priya (JIRA SRE-4219). Target: 2027-08-06.
  * Add a dashboard panel for per-client prefix churn within `infra/observability/prefix-cache`. Owner: Maya. Target: 2027-08-05.
  * Runbook edit: add checklist for "identify aggressive prefixes by client tag" and remediation steps (draft below).

Incident 2 — P2: autoscaler controller degraded (21:10–21:47)
- Symptoms: delayed scale-up events for dedicated pools causing transient queueing in dedicated-tier app pods. Alert: `controller.autoscaler.sync-latency:warn`
- Mitigation sequence:
  1) 21:12 — restarted autoscaler controller pod on cluster5 (kubectl rollout restart deployment/autoscaler-controller -n infra).
  2) 21:20 — promoted standby controller (leader election fallback) via `kubectl annotate` to force leader handover; effective at 21:26.
  3) 21:30 — manually triggered scale-up for impacted node pool to satisfy backlog.
- Root cause hypothesis: a race in leader election code surfaced under a control-plane API flapping event from a cloud provider region (ticket opened with provider: CLOUD-2983).
- Followups / Actions:
  * Patch PR for autoscaler leader election timeout bump — owner: Ethan Ross (linked PR in repo). Testing in staging scheduled 2027-08-04.
  * Add a QoS-based escalation step in runbook to promote standby earlier. Owner: Maya. Target: 2027-08-07.

Operational notes / Observability checklist (what to check immediately on start):
- Grafana dashboards to open: `Prod / Inference / Cache Overview`, `Prod / Autoscaler / Control Plane`, `Prod / API / Tail Latency by Route`.
- Important metrics: prefix_cache_eviction_rate, kv_cache_hit_ratio, autoscaler_sync_lag_ms, queue_depth_per_route, request_5xx_rate.
- Logs to tail: `kubectl logs -n inference deploy/prefix-cache -f --tail=200` and `kubectl logs -n infra deploy/autoscaler-controller -f --tail=200`.
- Quick k8s commands: 
  * kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep prefix-cache
  * kubectl describe hpa -n infra autoscaler-controller
  * curl -sS "https://obs-api.redwood-internal/api/v1/query?query=prefix_cache_eviction_rate" | jq '.'

Runbook draft snippets (please incorporate into main runbook `infra/runbooks/cache-thrashing.md`):
- Title: Identify and mitigate prefix-cache thrash
- Trigger conditions: prefix_cache_eviction_rate > 20% sustained for >=5m OR kv_cache_hit_ratio < 0.7 AND request tail latency > 95th baseline
- Immediate steps:
  1) Identify top 5 clients by eviction events (use logs tag `client_id` or `token_owner`).
  2) Temporarily increase cache TTL: set `cache.prefix.ttl=600s` via feature-flag system.
  3) If evictions persist, add capacity: scale prefix-cache deployment by +30% (or +3 pods).
  4) Notify solutions-eng and account team for client throttling/mitigation.
- Postmortem notes required: include client IDs, changed TTL value, duration, and confirm whether PR is needed to change defaults.

Outstanding tasks & owners (short list):
- Priya: finalize PR SRE-4219 to update TTL default and add unit test for TTL boundary. (ETA 2027-08-06)
- Ethan: complete autoscaler leader-election PR and coordinate staging validation (ETA 2027-08-04)
- Maya: add dashboard panel and draft runbook edits (ETA 2027-08-05)
- Liam: night watch — monitor spikes between 00:00–04:00 PST; escalate to Priya if eviction_rate > 30% for 10m.

Communication & customer notes:
- No customer-facing incidents today. Solutions-eng notified for the client observed in cache thrash; account manager Suresh K. aware and prepping a short heads-up if we opt to throttle.

Hand-off checklist for Liam (incoming):
- Read above incidents and open `infra/observability/prefix-cache` dashboard at shift start.
- Confirm autoscaler controller leader status: `kubectl get lease -n infra` and validate `autoscaler-controller` leader with timestamp.
- Keep eyes on the live alert `svc-inference.cache-eviction-rate:high` (pager set). If it fires twice within 30m, escalate to Priya directly and call out to oncall rotation.
- If you need to apply TTL bump, follow runbook snippet and file a follow-up PR referencing SRE-4219.

Notes to future reviewer (Maya):
- I'm leaving some raw queries in the runbook draft; please tidy the PromQL and add per-client groupings. The per-client log tag names are inconsistent across older clients — we should standardize `client_id` vs `token_owner` in logs.
- Consider adding a client-side best-practices doc for prefix usage (cc: product/SDK).

Raw links and artifacts:
- JIRA SRE-4219 (cache TTL PR)
- JIRA SRE-4221 (autoscaler flapping investigation)
- GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/739 (backoff -> leader election timeout bump)
- Confluence note (draft runbook): https://confluence.internal.redwood/infra/runbooks/cache-thrashing (draft)

End of handoff. Ping me on Slack (@mchen) for anything urgent; phone available. Good luck.
